source.title: A Comparison of Optimization Algorithms for Deep Learning

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer training recipes and held-out performance on natural image datasets, a conceptual test of V4. It does not test random-label memorization or the other mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy for ten optimizers across three CNN architectures and four datasets. Rows retain SGD and the highest-test-accuracy adaptive optimizer for each dataset and architecture; other optimizer results are summarized in rows_left_out. Training-loss curves and training-time comparisons are not extracted as gap measures.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers with SGD and momentum variants using held-out image-classification performance. This tests V4 under a narrow, fixed training recipe, although it does not establish performance after systematic learning-rate and schedule tuning.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: the authors describe adaptive methods as mostly superior and computationally efficient, with generally better results on the supervised and unsupervised tasks examined. This is their overall interpretation, not a claim that every adaptive method wins every comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Compares standard gradient optimizers on image classification with fixed batch size and epochs; reports test accuracy rather than training-to-test gaps. Learning rates are selected for best test results.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and CNN architecture change the optimizer rankings and test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Autoencoder reconstruction and denoising results favor Adam variants in many conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects image reconstruction performance; this is outside V4's classification and language benchmark claim.

record.peer_reviewed: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: No random-label or memorization-capacity test; no explicit training/test error-gap analysis; no reported uncertainty estimates. Hyperparameters are selected for best test results, limiting interpretation of test-set comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: The additional optimizer entries in Tables 3–6 (SGD momentum, SGD Nesterov, AdaGrad, AdaDelta, RMSProp, Adam, AdaMax, Nadam, AMSGrad) are omitted where not selected as SGD or the highest-test-accuracy adaptive method. The paper also reports unsupervised reconstruction losses in Tables 7–10, which do not measure held-out classification generalization in V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, systematic learning-rate and decay-schedule searches, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and the equal-or-better-training-performance qualification. Training curves are discussed, but their numerical endpoints are unavailable in the supplied text.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout ablations, training-set-size dependence, and removal alongside weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

missing.what: Test cross-entropy for the retained SGD/adaptive pairs. Its ranking sometimes opposes accuracy: SGD has lower loss on CIFAR-10 CNN-2/CNN-3 and Flowers CNN-1/CNN-2, whereas the retained adaptive winner has lower loss in the other eight pairs.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is not an original source for V4. Learning rates are fixed at 0.01 for SGD variants and 0.001 for adaptive methods; hyperparameters were chosen using test results, with no systematic search or decay schedule reported. Initialization, batch size and epoch budget are shared; weight decay and dropout are applied. No uncertainty estimates establish significance of the small MNIST differences. Selecting the best adaptive optimizer exaggerates any inference about adaptive methods as a class, and plain SGD understates the stronger momentum baselines already declared omitted in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same architectures and recipes.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; Adam on word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons and fixed epoch budget effects.
Dropout ablations and comparisons with augmentation.
Sharpness and other measured properties as predictors of generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Test accuracy of the retained best adaptive optimizer versus plain SGD, across all four datasets and three CNNs, after 50 epochs
relationships.reason: R1–R24 show higher adaptive accuracy in every retained pair, by 0.18–65.09 percentage points; these are selected winners under fixed learning rates, not evidence that every adaptive optimizer wins.
relationships.display_finding: The selected adaptive winners exceeded SGD accuracy in every retained comparison by 0.18–65.09 percentage points, with hyperparameters selected using test performance.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Test accuracy of the retained best adaptive optimizer versus plain SGD, across all four datasets and three CNNs, after 50 epochs
source_check.reason: Tables 3–6 confirm higher adaptive accuracy in all twelve retained pairs, by 0.18–65.09 percentage points. This reversal applies to the selected winners and stated recipe.

relationships.condition: Test cross-entropy for the retained adaptive winners on CIFAR-10 CNN-2/CNN-3 and Flowers CNN-1/CNN-2
relationships.reason: Based on table text missing from the accuracy rows: adaptive versus SGD losses are 1.1240/0.8899, 1.0437/1.0112, 1.8220/1.0115 and 1.1429/1.0764, respectively; adaptive accuracy improves while held-out loss worsens.
relationships.display_finding: The reported combination of higher adaptive accuracy and worse test cross-entropy remains unverified, with hyperparameters selected using test performance.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Test cross-entropy for the retained adaptive winners on CIFAR-10 CNN-2/CNN-3 and Flowers CNN-1/CNN-2
source_check.reason: Tables 4 and 6 confirm worse adaptive test cross-entropy: 1.1240 versus 0.8899, 1.0437 versus 1.0112, 1.8220 versus 1.0115, and 1.1429 versus 1.0764. These loss results support V4 despite higher accuracy.

relationships.condition: Test cross-entropy for the retained adaptive winners on MNIST, LFW, CIFAR-10 CNN-1 and Flowers CNN-3
relationships.reason: Based on Tables 3–6, missing loss rows show lower adaptive test loss in these eight comparisons, agreeing with their accuracy advantage.
relationships.display_finding: The selected adaptive winners reportedly had lower test cross-entropy in the eight specified comparisons, but these loss comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.reason: Tables 3–6 confirm lower adaptive test cross-entropy in all eight specified comparisons, reversing the worse-held-out-performance effect for these selected winners.

relation.reason: Its own optimizer comparisons directly measure the held-out performance named in V4.

tranche.reason: The study compares adaptive and nonadaptive optimizers on held-out image-classification performance using its own CNN architectures and fixed training recipe, addressing V4 through a different experimental method.

source_check.notes: Section 4.2 selects hyperparameters using test performance; systematic learning-rate or schedule searches and uncertainty estimates are not reported. The retained rows select accuracy winners; loss rankings differ, and these held-out results alone do not establish train–test gaps.

reader_labels.reason: Adaptive methods usually have higher reported test accuracy than SGD in the retained comparisons, but the study does not isolate generalization gaps and chooses hyperparameters for best test results; see R1–R24.
